title: Cinder Analytics integration scratchpad
body:
Meeting: Intro + tech deep dive with Cinder Analytics (2025-11-02)
Attendees: Ava M (Redwood SE), Liam C (Redwood), Samir R (Redwood), Priya N (Cinder CTO), Rob K (Cinder infra lead)

Summary / context:
Cinder is a mid-market analytics vendor embedding an LLM-powered semantic search + automated summarization into their managed on-prem appliance for enterprise customers. They want a hybrid deployment: Redwood Private (on-prem package) as primary inference for PII-heavy customers, but automatic failover to Hosted API for non-PII or for burst capacity. Their current appliance runs on 2xA100 (40GB) per box and an off-box aggregator. They prefer minimal changes to their appliance image.

Key asks / requirements (explicit):
- P99 generation latency target: 150ms for top-k semantic reranking (embedding similarity + lightweight reranker).
- Batch search throughput: sustain ~1000 queries/min per appliance during peak (spiky distribution).
- Data residency: customer data must never leave their VPC for regulated customers (set of named customers).
- KMS/HSM integration: must support their AWS CloudHSM + customer-managed keys for logs and checkpoints.
- Model pinning: ability to pin a quantized LLM + an embedding model at the tenant level and stage rollouts.
- Audit logs: retention 12 months, searchable for request->response trace by request_id.
- Fallback behavior: auto-failover to Redwood Hosted only for non-sensitive tenants; they want simple routing policy.

Notes from tech discussion (raw):
- They currently use a small faiss index + on-disk vector store; plan is to move to a memory-backed index in the appliance to reduce disk IO. Concern: memory pressure when KV cache + index + model resident in 40GB GPU memory.
- Rob: "We don't want to recompile the appliance kernel" -> preference for shipping Redwood runtime container with compatibility shim.
- Priya: worried about maintenance overhead if we require too many bespoke changes per customer appliance; asks for a single supported bundle.
- We discussed quantization tradeoffs: int8/llm.int4 profiles likely needed to fit larger models in 40GB; embedding model separate on CPU if cheaper.
- Observability: they want per-tenant breakdowns in our console (latency & token cost) but also a local metrics sink (Prometheus) to integrate with their on-prem monitoring.

Gotchas / risks flagged:
- KV cache eviction semantics: if we enable shared prefix caching across tenants on the same appliance, risk of cross-tenant leakage unless strict isolation is enforced (prob not acceptable). Recommend tenant-scoped caches only.
- Failover latency: spinning up hosted fallback for many simultaneous tenants could cause a spike; need warm-pool or pre-provisioned dedicated capacity for their ARR profile.
- Disk + memory constraints: model + index + runtime might push beyond 40GB for the combo of embedding + LLM if not quantized; need explicit benchmark on their box.
- Networking constraints: some customers' appliances are air-gapped; fallback to hosted is impossible in those cases — need policy-level tagging.

Open questions to resolve with Cinder:
- Which tenants are "regulated" vs "non-regulated" (list and tagging process)?
- Expected distribution of short text vs long-context requests (this impacts optimistic kernel selection).
- Will they accept int8 quantized model for reranker? Or require fp16 for quality?
- Do they have an existing Prometheus pushgateway or should we provide a metrics exporter?

Action items / next steps (owners):
- Ava: create a capacity micro-benchmark plan to run on a 2xA100 (40GB) baseline image; include embeddings+reranker combos. Deliver by 2025-11-10.
- Liam: draft a private-deploy packaging option that uses a compatibility shim container (min changes to host); initial sketch by 2025-11-07.
- Samir: sketch the fallback routing policy implementation and warm-pool sizing heuristic; include runbook for per-tenant policies. Due 2025-11-12.
- Rob (Cinder): provide a sample tenant list and a small anonymized traffic trace (1 week) that shows peak QPS and request size distribution; due 2025-11-14.
- Joint: schedule a follow-up deep-dive (benchmark day) week of 2025-11-17; aim for a hands-on lab with Cinder infra team.

Quick sketch of benchmark plan (notes to self):
- Tests: single-request p99 latency, sustained throughput (QPS) with 95%ile latency target, memory/disk utilization, cold-start times for model swap, failover time to hosted endpoint.
- Workloads: 60% short queries (<128 tokens), 35% mid (128-512), 5% long (>512) to cover KV cache behavior.
- Model variants: small reranker (7B quantized int8), medium (13B int8), embedding on CPU (sentence-transformer equivalent).
- Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU memory breakdown (model, cache, temp), CPU load, network egress (to detect unintentional calls).

Notes to include in proposal draft (sales collateral):
- Emphasize our "unified runtime" message — same API and rollout controls whether on-prem or Hosted.
- Highlight warm-pool approach for predictable failover.
- Call out tenant-scoped cache isolation as a security-first design choice.

Draft epilogue (for internal sync):
This is an early-stage integration that materially touches Private packaging, routing, and billing (because warm-pools cost). Keep the SE + product + support loop in the thread. Prioritize a short concrete benchmark run — that will answer the biggest unknowns (memory fit, latency at p99, and necessary quantization).

Random personal notes / scratch thoughts:
- Consider offering a "private-lite" SKU: smaller supported bundle that limits model size but lowers operational complexity (fits in their current appliance without kernel changes). Could be an on-ramp.
- Might propose a configurable fallback policy UI in console: toggle per-tenant: never/allowed-with-approval/allowed-automatically.

Last sync: 2025-11-04 (quick internal huddle) — aligned on owners.
